summary.text: LaKesha Womack is the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 14th Congressional District. A Charlotte-area consultant and ordained minister, she is Chief Strategy Officer at ASPIRE Community Capital and has worked on political campaigns. She describes her campaign priorities as affordable health care, economic mobility, equitable education, and strengthening democratic participation.

paragraphs.text: Earned a high school diploma from the Alabama School of Math and Science and a bachelor's degree from Vanderbilt University in 1999; is pursuing a Master of Legal Studies at Vanderbilt Law School.

Describes herself as the owner of Womack Consulting Group, which she says has provided strategic advisory services to nonprofits, small businesses, faith-based organizations, and political campaigns for more than two decades.

Career experience includes working as a consultant, deacon, Chief Strategy Officer at ASPIRE Community Capital (a community development financial institution), and CEO at Thrive Creative Community; affiliated with Friends of Keep Charlotte Beautiful, Charlotte Business INClusion Advisory Committee, and Black Seed Network.

Says her political experience includes working on Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign, serving on the Podium Operations Team for the 2024 Democratic National Convention, and working as a strategist for local and state-level campaigns.
Says she is an ordained minister in the African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church and has completed The Campaign School at Yale, Emerge America, and Lead NC.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.2% of the vote over Brent Caldwell and Ahmid Kargbo.
